title: Anthropological investigation of burial practices in Greco-Roman Egypt
abstract: Death has long been regarded as one of the most influential aspects of human existence, shaping religious beliefs, cultural traditions, and social institutions across different civilizations. Funeral customs and mortuary rituals are not merely responses to death; rather, they represent complex cultural practices through which societies express their perceptions of life, the afterlife, and the relationship between the living and the deceased. From an anthropological perspective, funerary practices provide valuable evidence for understanding social organization, cultural identity, collective memory, and symbolic systems that govern human behavior.( )Among ancient civilizations, Egypt developed one of the most sophisticated and enduring funerary traditions. Egyptian religious thought regarded death as the beginning of a new stage of existence rather than the end of life. Consequently, preserving the body through mummification, performing funerary ceremonies, and providing the deceased with protective texts and burial equipment were considered essential requirements for achieving eternal life. These beliefs were firmly established through religious compositions such as the Pyramid Texts, the Coffin Texts, and the Book of the Dead, all of which provided theological guidance for the deceased during the journey to the afterlife.
venue: Al-Mağallah Al-ʿilmiyyaẗ Li Kulliyyaẗ Al-Adāb - Ǧāmiʿaẗ Asyūṭ/Al-Mağallah Al-ʿilmiyyaẗ Li Kulliyyaẗ Al-Adāb - Ǧāmiʿaẗ Asyūṭ

title: DIFFERENCES IN CULTURAL INTERPRETATION AND AESTHETIC DEPICTION OF WARTIME EXPERIENCE
abstract: This article examines the differences in the cultural interpretation and aesthetic representation of wartime experience in various literary and artistic traditions. It focuses on the ways in which war, heroism, sacrifice, trauma, death, national identity, and collective memory are represented through literature, cinema, and visual art. Particular attention is paid to the differences between Western European, American, Russian, and Central Asian approaches to depicting wartime reality. The study demonstrates that artistic representations of war are strongly influenced by historical circumstances, cultural values, ideological perspectives, religious beliefs, and social traditions. While some works portray war through the concepts of heroism, patriotism, and collective sacrifice, others emphasize individual suffering, psychological trauma, moral ambiguity, civilian losses, and the consequences of violence. The article also considers the transformation of wartime aesthetics from traditional heroic narratives to modern and postmodern forms characterized by fragmentation, documentary realism, multiple perspectives, and silence. It argues that the comparative study of wartime representations provides a deeper understanding of how different societies remember historical events, construct cultural identity, and transmit traumatic experiences from one generation to another.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ НАЦИОНАЛЬНЫХ ОБРЯДОВ УЗБЕКСКОГО НАРОДА В XX — НАЧАЛЕ XXI ВЕКА: ИСТОРИОГРАФИЧЕСКИЙ АНАЛИЗ
abstract: The article presents a historiographical analysis of studies devoted to the transformation of the national rituals of the Uzbek people in the twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. It examines the main approaches to the study of family and domestic, wedding, birth, funeral and commemorative, calendar, and economic rituals in Soviet, post-Soviet Uzbek, and foreign historiography. The study demonstrates that scholarly approaches to traditional rituals changed depending on the socio-political and methodological context. In Soviet ethnography, transformations of ritual practices were predominantly interpreted within the concepts of the “new way of life,” the elimination of religious survivals, and the formation of socialist rituals. Following Uzbekistan’s independence, scholarly attention shifted toward historical continuity, ethnocultural identity, religious beliefs, local specificities, and the revival of traditional cultural elements. In contemporary foreign historiography, the transformation of ritual practices is analyzed through the perspectives of traditionalization, social modernization, legal pluralism, consumer culture, state regulation, and changes in local social institutions. Particular attention is given to studies based on materials from the Fergana Valley. The analysis demonstrates that, despite a substantial body of research devoted to individual types of rituals, a comprehensive historical reconstruction of their transformation throughout the Soviet and post-Soviet periods remains insufficiently developed.
venue: Ijtimoiy-gumanitar sohada ilmiy-innovatsion tadqiqotlar

title: Marital Stressors and Management of Psychological Problems in Mariama Ba’s So Long a Letter
abstract: This study examines how marital conditions trigger psychological problems in African cultural society, focusing on Mariama Ba’s So Long a Letter. It also explores the underlying causes and management strategies of emotional pains in socio-cultural settings. The study adopted Freudian Psychoanalytic theory that focuses on the causality of the psychic and emotional conflicts being experienced by individuals in society. The findings revealed that betrayal of trust, economic hardship, untimely death, intra-family pressure, family background, co-wife antagonism, religious beliefs and traditional practices are serious marital stressors that trigger psychological and emotional problems in marriages/family units in African society. These stressors have some adverse effects on patients, including depression, phobic anxieties, insomnia, posttraumatic stress disorders, behaviour disorders, and so on. The study also found that psychological suffering is managed in several ways, such as writing, adjustment strategies, distractive techniques, sublimation, medical treatment, etc. The research concludes that couples should be faithful to their partners, ensures mutual understanding and never allows family pressure and customary laws and practices to interfere in their marriages. However, where there are stressors, couples should endeavour to adopt effective coping strategies to promote marital health and improve quality of life.
venue: International Journal of Literature Language and Linguistics

title: A comunicação médico-paciente na perspectiva de médicas residentes: estudo de caso
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Communication skills are essential for comprehensive care and quality of care in healthcare institutions. OBJECTIVE: This research aimed to understand the perception of medical residents regarding the challenges of communication in hospital routine and to investigate their repertoire of interpersonal communication skills in patient and family care. METHOD: A multiple case study was developed with two physicians enrolled in the residency program of a federal hospital located in Rio de Janeiro. Self-administered questionnaires were administered, and two individual sessions were conducted with each participant, consisting of a semi-structured interview and discussion of clinical cases. The data were subjected to Content Analysis. RESULTS: The categories generated showed challenges related to management (abuse of hierarchies, moral harassment), services (pressure for productivity, overload of activities and limited time), users (resistance, low education, religious beliefs), and the professionals themselves (lack of technical preparation, emotional exhaustion, boundaries in bonding). The residents positively evaluated their social and communication skills but pointed out difficulties regarding clarity in giving instructions and emotional regulation. FINAL CONSIDERATIONS: It is hoped that the data generated by studies such as this can support professional education actions capable of contributing to a greater humanization of services in the hospital setting and improving communication quality in healthcare.
venue: Revista Psicologia Diversidade e Saúde

title: Reassessing the Orans Pose in Roman Egyptian Funerary Art: Two Unpublished Stelae from Mendes
abstract: This study presents, for the first time, two funerary stelae from ancient Mendes (Dakahlia) while aiming to date and interpret them. It also compares these stelae with similar examples from Kom Abu Bellou and Roman-era sarcophagi, tracing their origins and examining the continuity of their design into the Coptic and Christian artistic contexts. The research explores the intended meaning of the raisedhand gesture of the deceased on these stelae, emphasizing the orans posture and relating it to the prevailing religious beliefs of the time. The analysis indicates that the owners of the two stelae were not necessarily Egyptian; however, they were clearly influenced by ancient Egyptian religious concepts, including the depiction of funerary deities such as Anubis. Furthermore, the study shows that the orans posture served as a visual tool, expressing the moral identity of the deceased and their successful passage through divine judgment, in line with Greco-Roman notions of pietas. This approach reflects a hybrid strategy, preserving Egyptian funerary ideology while visually adapting it to be comprehensible within a multicultural environment. In conclusion, the artistic culture in Mendes during the Roman period maintained the continuity of Egyptian funerary practices through the conscious adaptation of traditional symbols and techniques. This reflects a productive interaction between local heritage and classical influences in shaping the posthumous identity of the deceased.
venue: Historia i Świat

title: Sikh Youth in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry: A Clinical Perspective
abstract: Sikh children and adolescents represent a growing but understudied population in child and adolescent psychiatry. Many Sikh youth navigate complex intersections of religious identity, family expectations, migration experiences, and minority stress, particularly in diaspora contexts where visible articles of faith may increase vulnerability to discrimination and bullying. At the same time, strong family cohesion, community support, and religious values often function as important sources of resilience. This Clinical Perspectives article reviews key cultural and developmental considerations relevant to Sikh youth, including core religious beliefs, family structure and intergenerational dynamics, acculturation processes, and experiences of stigma and help-seeking. Clinical assessment and treatment recommendations are discussed, with emphasis on cultural humility, family engagement, and recognition of both risk and protective factors. A clinical vignette illustrates how cultural, familial, and minority stress factors may influence presentation and treatment engagement. Greater awareness of Sikh cultural context can help clinicians build trust, reduce misinterpretation of culturally normative behaviors, and provide more effective, culturally responsive care. These principles may also inform work with other youth from visible religious and ethnic minority backgrounds.
venue: JAACAP Connect

title: Liberation Through Contextualization: African Women’s Theology and the Trokosi System within the Ewe Culture of Ghana”
abstract: This article delves into African women’s theologies, specifically analyzing the intersection of cultural practices and religious beliefs as exemplified by the Trokosi system among some Ewe people of Ghana, exploring how the Trokosi system reflects broader theological issues regarding creation and humanity within an African context, framed through biblical revelation. Recognizing African women’s theologies as a dynamic and critical movement, this research advocates for a re-evaluation of both established church practices and cultural norms that perpetuate gender inequality. It posits African feminist cultural hermeneutic as a fundamental process through which the gospel can elevate and transform negative cultural phenomena, advocating for the promotion of cultural values that positively influence society while critically rejecting harmful narratives. However, it recognizes the importance of preserving certain cultural narratives integral to African and women’s identities, resisting the notion of wholesale abandonment of cultural heritage. Drawing from the works of notable African women theologians, the study highlights the significance of women’s experiences in shaping their theological perspectives and emphasizes the necessity of a partnership between men and women within the broader human community. Ultimately, the article calls for a renewed commitment to gendering contextualization, fostering inculturation that promotes justice, equality, and communal flourishing.
venue: African Christian Theology.

title: MAINSTREAM CHRISTIAN CHURCHES AND SEXUAL DIVERSITY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF ATTITUDES, PRACTICES, AND INCLUSION OF GAY AND LESBIAN COMMUNITIES
authors: Ramohlale P.P, Chauke O.R, Ramogale P and Ramohlale M.I.
abstract: Mainstream Christian churches are long-established and institutionally recognised denominations that have played a significant role in shaping religious beliefs and practices in South Africa. These include the Roman Catholic, Anglican, Methodist, Lutheran, and Presbyterian churches. This study critically examines the attitudes, practices, and approaches of these churches towards lesbian and gay communities within the context of South Africa's constitutional commitment to equality and non-discrimination. A qualitative research approach, guided by a case study design, was employed to explore the perspectives and experiences of church leaders and congregants. Data were collected through focus group discussions and document analysis. The findings indicate that mainstream Christian churches continue to grapple with the challenges posed by sexual diversity, particularly regarding the recognition and blessing of same-sex marriages, the participation of lesbian and gay individuals in church leadership and worship, and the acceptance of diverse gender expression. These issues reflect the broader tension between adherence to traditional theological doctrines and the demands of an inclusive constitutional democracy. The study concludes that mainstream Christian churches remain engaged in an ongoing process of negotiating the balance between preserving doctrinal integrity and responding to evolving societal expectations for inclusion and equal treatment of lesbian and gay communities.
venue: Journal of Research Administration

title: Fostering institutional trust and organ donation: Evidence from a randomized informational intervention in Tunisia
abstract: Organ transplantation saves lives and improves the quality of life of patients who would otherwise depend on costly and invasive treatments. The technology is becoming available in low- and middle-income countries, but the gap between the demand for and the supply of organ transplants remains large. In a randomized controlled trial at a Tunisian university, we evaluate an expert-led intervention designed to inform about organ donation and strengthen trust in medical institutions. The intervention consists of a short video testimonial from a heart transplant survivor, a presentation led by a medical doctor and a short Q&A session. We find that the intervention significantly increases deceased donor registration, with suggestive evidence of positive spillover effects on the control group. The survey data provides little support for changes in attitudes and social expectations as potential mechanisms. Instead, it reveals large and statistically significant increases in medical and legal knowledge, religious beliefs supportive of donation, and institutional trust among treated students. Finally, we show that treatment effects on organ donor registration are driven by male students and those whose families likely support organ donation. Targeting older segments of the population may further increase the impact and cost-effectiveness of this intervention.
venue: Journal of Development Economics

title: Rose
abstract: Abstract This chapter tells the story of Rose, a forty-five-year-old South Sudanese mother living in the Kalobeyei settlement, whose household lies at the tenth percentile of the Kakuma income distribution. Rose is amongst the poorest in the camps. She fled South Sudan in 2016 with her four children but without her husband. Like many women in Kakuma, she never attended school and has no formal employment. Her one-room home shelters the entire family. She keeps ducks, which she sometimes sells to buy food for her children. Fully dependent on humanitarian assistance, she has accumulated unsustainable debt as shopkeepers, acting as informal lenders, retain refugees’ ATM cards as collateral and charge inflated prices. Her story also reflects broader challenges in Kalobeyei, including limited electricity, severe water scarcity, and the fragile coexistence between refugees and Turkana hosts. Yet, she is also hopeful for the future, wants her children to be able to access education, and has strong religious beliefs. Her story reveals that circumstances can change over time; she had found a job when we met again in Kakuma two years later.

title: อตลกษณชาวจนมาเลเซยในบรบทพหวฒนธรรม
abstract: This study investigates the development of Chinese identity in Malaysia within the context of a multicultural state, focusing on the period from the major Chinese migration in the 19th century to the post-independence era. A qualitative research methodology was employed, based on the study of literature, historical documents, and academic works. The analysis applies the theoretical frameworks of Situational Ethnicity and Labeling Theory to understand the dynamics of identity formation shaped externally by the state and social structures, as well as internally by the agency of the Chinese community itself.The findings reveal that Chinese identity in Malaysia is not fixed but is a continuously negotiated and evolving process. This is evident across four dimensions: (1) Ethnicity – the Peranakan group displays a hybrid Chinese–Malay identity depending on context; (2) Politics – Chinese identity has shifted from being China-oriented to Malaya-oriented; (3) Religion – Chinese Christians negotiate between traditional culture and new religious beliefs; and (4) Education – Chinese schools serve as sites for reproducing Chinese identity and negotiating with state policies.These findings demonstrate that Chinese identity in Malaysia is shaped by dynamic interactions between individuals, communities, and the state. A comprehensive understanding of this identity thus requires attention to both structural forces and lived experiences.
venue: Journal of Graduate School Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University

title: Widowhood and loneliness in Haulawng community
abstract: Bereavement, the loss of a primary source of social and emotional support, alteration in roles and living arrangements defines the horrendous period of widowhood. This study attempts to explore the levels of loneliness during widowhood and analyzing the relationship between support network, coping mechanism and loneliness among widows and widowers. The study is an exploratory research design. The sample size is 30 in which stratified simple random sampling method is used to collect data. The levels of loneliness, support network and coping mechanism are measured. The result of the study indicates that the mean age is 66.66 among which Christianity is a predominant religious belief where majority practice joint family system. The respondents receive positive support from their significant dear ones, community and government services. The data shows that the level of loneliness falls in high category in which widowers are more. There is a significant difference between widows and widowers with regards to coping styles. The study shows that there is significant correlation between loneliness, coping mechanism, support network, time spent with and gender. The study highlights the need for improved psycho-social support both at the professional and community level for widows and widowers. Future research should continue to explore the immediate effects of bereavement and coping to understand the psycho-social impact.
venue: International Journal of Sociology and Humanities

title: Married Women’s Perception of Family Planning Techniques and Implications for Population Growth in Nigeria: Study of Lagelu LGA, Oyo State
abstract: This study examined married women’s perception of family planning techniques and the implications for population growth in Nigeria, using Lagelu Local Government Area of Oyo State as a case study. The research adopted a descriptive survey design, employing structured questionnaires and interviews to collect data from 520 married women randomly selected across 13 wards that constitute the Local Government Area. Data were analyzed using tables, cross tabulation, percentages and descriptive methods of data analysis. Findings revealed that awareness of modern family planning methods was high in the study area, but actual utilization was limited by spousal disapproval, religious beliefs, fear of infertility, fear of promiscuity and fear of side effects. The study further established a significant relationship between women’s perception of family planning and their fertility behavior, indicating that negative perceptions contribute to high fertility rates and rapid population growth in the area. However, the recommendations put forward include establishment of more functional family planning clinics, more jingles on radio using local language, consistent supply of contraceptives by governments and NGOs, sensitization programme to make men to see the need for family planning techniques among others.
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: KONFLIK SOSIAL ANTARA NORMA MAYORITAS DAN IDENTITAS MINORITAS MUSLIM DALAM NOVEL LANGIT GORYEO KARYA BERLIANA KIMBERLY: TINJAUAN SOSIOLOGI SASTRA PERSPEKTIF PIERRE BOURDIEU
abstract: ABSTRACT Social conflict between majority norms and Muslim minority identity in literary works can reveal how individual beliefs encounter dominant social rules. This study analyzes the representation of such conflict and the relationship between habitus, field, capital, and symbolic power in shaping the position of characters in Berliana Kimberly’s novel Langit Goryeo. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach, using the novel as the data source and collecting data in the form of words, phrases, sentences, dialogues, and narratives related to social conflict and identity negotiation. Data were collected through documentation and note-taking, while the analysis involved data reduction, classification, interpretation, and conclusion drawing. Analysis of six main data units revealed four prominent forms of conflict: tensions surrounding religious practices in social interactions, restrictions on interactions based on religious beliefs, family conflict concerning marital choices, and clashes over values related to family and descendants. Conflict emerges when the character’s religious habitus encounters a social field governed by different norms, while support from the Muslim community serves as social capital for maintaining identity. Identity negotiation occurs through rejecting practices that contradict religious beliefs, adjusting to social relationships, and participating in the Muslim community. These findings are limited to the social representation constructed within a single novel. ABSTRACT Konflik sosial antara norma mayoritas dan identitas minoritas Muslim dalam karya sastra dapat memperlihatkan bagaimana keyakinan individu berhadapan dengan aturan sosial yang dominan. Penelitian ini menganalisis representasi konflik tersebut serta hubungan antara habitus, arena, modal, dan kekuasaan simbolik yang membentuk posisi tokoh dalam novel Langit Goryeo karya Berliana Kimberly. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan sumber data berupa novel dan data berupa kata, frasa, kalimat, dialog, serta narasi yang berkaitan dengan konflik sosial dan negosiasi identitas. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui dokumentasi dan pencatatan, sedangkan analisis mencakup reduksi, klasifikasi, interpretasi, dan penarikan simpulan. Hasil penelitian terhadap enam data utama memperlihatkan empat bentuk konflik yang menonjol, yaitu pertentangan praktik keagamaan dalam pergaulan, pembatasan interaksi berdasarkan keyakinan, konflik keluarga terkait pilihan perkawinan, dan benturan nilai mengenai keluarga serta keturunan. Konflik muncul ketika habitus religius tokoh berhadapan dengan arena sosial yang menetapkan norma berbeda, sementara dukungan komunitas Muslim menjadi sumber modal sosial bagi pemertahanan identitas. Negosiasi identitas berlangsung melalui penolakan terhadap praktik yang bertentangan dengan keyakinan, penyesuaian dalam relasi sosial, dan keterlibatan dalam komunitas Muslim. Temuan ini terbatas pada representasi sosial dalam satu novel.
venue: LANGUAGE Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Bahasa dan Sastra

title: Conceptions of God and Epistemic Mediation: A Five-Layer Model Abstract Religious
abstract: This article presents a five-layer architecture for determining the scope of epistemic revision in religious belief: formation, conception, propositional attitude, justification, and truth/reference. Its scope-dependency principle states that a finding at one layer warrants revision at another only through a specified connection; once such dependence is established, layer distinctions do not insulate the dependent claim. The architecture is not itself theistic. A worked application conditionally adopts theistic realism and analogical divine consciousness while separating creation, relation, revelation, and communicative trustworthiness. Sources are assessed through reliability, conditional independence, alternative explanations, and defeaters rather than source type. Worked cases distinguish lost corroboration from lost total support, available grounds from actual bases for belief, and false attribution from failed reference. Propositional and doxastic justification remain distinct, as do personal and public justification. The contribution is a typed assessment record and a criterion of diagnostic adequacy: an assessment of revision must identify its target, dependency, required response, and residual uncertainty. Each coordinate is task-relative and non-redundant in the worked cases. A proposition-centered checklist is equivalent only insofar as it represents these same distinctions and links; comparative practical performance remains to be tested.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Dispassion as a Common State of Mind for Liberation in Buddhism and Hinduism
abstract: Dispassion (Vairāgya/Virāga) has been considered an essential notion in Hinduism and Buddhism for attaining a complete liberation from suffering. The main objective of the study, is to analyze how the practice of Vairāgya/Virāga leads one to liberation in Hindu and Buddhist philosophies. The method of study chosen for conducting the research is qualitative comparative analysis of religious texts including but not limited to the Bhagavad Gītā and Upaniṣads along with texts in Pāli Canon. The study investigates the concept, practice, and significance of Dispassion in each philosophy through thematic analysis. Both religions have been found agreeing with attachment or craving as a source of dukkha. However, there are significant differences in their ideas on the metaphysical aspect of non-attachment. In Hinduism, Vairāgya is a spiritual practicewhich leads to the realization of the Ātman and its relation to Brahman. In Buddhism, virāga arises through the realization of the three characteristics of existence: anicca, dukkha, and anattā. This realization leads to the renunciation of worldly attachments that hinder a Dhamma practitioner from attaining nirvāṇa. Consequently, in spite of being identical from the standpoint of morality, there exists an ontological gap between both religions concerning nonattachment. Thus, it may be said that non-attachment is both the common with distinguishing feature of the two religious beliefs. Such knowledge helps us better understand the doctrine of the East and highlight the significance of non-attachment as a remedy for modern psychological disorders.
venue: Dhammacakka Journal of Buddhism and Applied Buddhism

title: MUSLIM FAMILIES AND RELIGIOUS RESOURCES IN DEVELOPING PARENTAL ACCEPTANCE OF CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES
abstract: Parental acceptance is a crucial component of family adaptation and psychological well-being in families of children with disabilities. This study aims to examine the role of Muslim family environments and religious attitude (RA) in shaping parental acceptance of children with disabilities within a religiously embedded cultural context. Using a quantitative correlational design, data were collected from 77 parents of children with disabilities in Indonesia. The study focuses on key family-based factors, including parental understanding, social support, and Islamic religious beliefs as significant contributors to parental acceptance. The findings reveal that parental understanding (β = .34), Religious Attitude (RA) (β = .29), and social support (β = .25) significantly predict parental acceptance, jointly explaining 48% of the variance. These results indicate that parental acceptance is not solely determined by cognitive factors but is also shaped by social and faith-based resources within Muslim family environments. Islamic values, such as patience (ṣabr – صَبْر), gratitude (shukr – شُكْر), and trust in God (tawakkul – تَوَكُّل), provide meaningful frameworks that support parents in interpreting and accepting their child’s condition. The study implies that integrating Islamic values, strengthening parental understanding, and enhancing social support systems can contribute to more adaptive family processes and improved well-being among families of children with disabilities.
venue: EDURELIGIA JURNAL PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM

title: RELIGIOUS COPING AND CAREGIVER STRESS: SOCIOLOGICAL INSIGHTS INTO DOMESTIC CARE PRACTICES
abstract: Family caregiving is an essential yet demanding responsibility that is often accompanied by emotional, physical, and psychological stress. Religious beliefs and practices play a significant role in shaping how caregivers interpret their experiences and cope with the burdens of care in many households. This study examines the sociological dimensions of religious coping among family caregivers, highlighting the influence of faith-based frameworks on stress perception, caregiving roles, and help-seeking behaviors within domestic care settings. Religious coping may serve as a source of emotional strength, offering meaning, hope, and resilience during periods of strain. Prayer, communal support, and reliance on spiritual interpretations of illness can provide comfort and a sense of shared purpose. However, when caregivers feel spiritually inadequate, religious coping may also reinforce self-sacrifice, limit the pursuit of external support, or contribute to guilt. Through a sociological lens, this study explores the interplay between religion, household dynamics, and caregiving expectations, emphasizing how cultural and spiritual values shape the caregiving experience. Understanding these dynamics is crucial for developing culturally sensitive interventions that support caregiver well-being while respecting religious and social contexts. The analysis underscores the need for holistic approaches in domestic care practices that integrate spiritual resources with practical and psychosocial support systems
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Analisis Yuridis Putusan Pengadilan Agama Jakarta Timur No. 1700/Pdt.G/2010/PAJT tentang Pengalihan Hak Asuh Anak karena Ibu Murtad Perspektif Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah
abstract: This study is motivated by the problem of applying ḥaḍānah law when a mother who initially embraced Islam returns to her previous religion (apostasy), as reflected in East Jakarta Religious Court Decision Number 1700/Pdt.G/2010/PAJT. This study analyzes the legal considerations in the decision concerning the transfer of ḥaḍānah to the father following the mother’s apostasy and examines them from the perspective of Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah. The study employs a normative juridical approach. The primary legal source is East Jakarta Religious Court Decision Number 1700/Pdt.G/2010/PAJT, while secondary sources include books, journals, legislation, and expert opinions relevant to ḥaḍānah and Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah. The findings show that the Panel of Judges transferred ḥaḍānah to the father by placing the mother’s apostasy and her parenting practices, which were considered potentially influential on the child’s religious beliefs, as dominant considerations. However, from the perspective of Maqāṣid al-Syarī‘ah, these considerations did not fully balance the protection of religion with the child’s safety, psychological development, and continuity of the relationship with the mother. Therefore, apostasy should not, in itself, constitute the sole basis for transferring ḥaḍānah without concrete evidence of a threat to the child’s religion, safety, and development; the determination of custody should instead be directed toward the child’s welfare and best interests.
venue: Al-fiqh

title: POST-COVID GRIEF AND FAMILY RESILIENCE: A SOCIORELIGIOUS INSIGHTS
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic generated unprecedented levels of loss, altering family structures, routines, and emotional stability. Many households continue to grapple with post-COVID grief, characterized by unresolved sorrow, psychological strain, and the long-term effects of disrupted social and economic conditions. This article examines how families navigate the lingering emotional consequences of the pandemic and highlights the socioreligious factors that shape resilience. Drawing on sociological perspectives, the study explores how grief manifests within households, how family roles adjust after loss, and how communities mediate support. It emphasizes the significance of religious beliefs, rituals, and communal practices as coping tools that help families reinterpret trauma, sustain hope, and rebuild social cohesion. Religious narratives, mourning rites, and faith-based support networks provide frameworks for meaning-making and emotional recovery. At the same time, the article acknowledges the limitations of religious coping, particularly when spiritual interpretations intensify guilt, helplessness, or fatalism. The analysis argues that family resilience emerges through the interplay of emotional bonds, adaptive coping strategies, spiritual practices, and supportive social environments. Understanding these socioreligious dynamics is essential for developing culturally sensitive interventions that strengthen family well-being in the post-pandemic era
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Dialogues Across Differences: Lessons from the Jaina Tradition on Conflict Resolution and Reconciliation
abstract: Contemporary society grapples with diverse values and socio-economic structural differences. These differences extend beyond subtle contextual nuances and strategic considerations, intruding into one’s first-person account and preferences. From its first-order mooring, these divergences ascend to higher-order manifestations, expressing themselves in distinct political perspectives, cultural practices, and religious beliefs. While such differences inevitably give rise to conflicts, a deeper analysis reveals that the core of rising conflict often lies in sectarian differences. Although various conflict resolution mechanisms have been employed to settle disputes, they often fail to yield enduring results. In this regard, the paper proposes interfaith dialogue as a promising approach for conflict resolution and reconciliation. The paper argues that interfaith dialogue is neither a debate nor a negotiation, but a sustained endeavour to break down the walls of difference. Furthermore, to ensure substantive outcomes, the dialogue must be firmly grounded in philosophical foundations that are value-laden and universally acknowledged. Against this backdrop, the paper introduces the Jaina philosophical tradition, specifically the principle of ‘non-absolutism’ (anekāntavāda) and the doctrine of ‘qualified assertion’ (syādvāda), as a coherent framework for dialogical engagements. Focusing on epistemic decentring, conditional articulation, and non-violent involvement, the Jaina framework pushes interfaith dialogue beyond conflict resolution towards conflict transformation.
venue: Religions

title: Polish General Social Survey, 1992-1999
abstract: The Polish General Social Survey (PGSS), conducted annually since 1992 through 1995 and later biennially, is design to measure opinions and social characteristics of Polish society. PGSS core variables include socioeconomic and demographic items with an emphasis on stratification measures (occupation, labor force status, education, income) of respondents and their spouses and parents. In addition, there are attitudinal variables concerning political opinions and ideology, national spending, religious beliefs, social inequality, job and occupational values, tolerance, educational values, attitudes toward other countries, traditional sex roles, family issues, abortion, and homosexuality. Other variables gauge subjective well-being, social class identification, satisfaction with different spheres of life, and confidence in public institutions. Respondents were also queried about their voting behavior, social interactions, religiosity, health, smoking, and drinking. Each year, additional topical modules of questions from the International Social Survey Program have been added: "Inequality II" (1992), "Environment" (1993), "Family and Changing Gender Roles II" and "Sexual Behavior" (1994), "National Identity" (1995), "Work Orientations II" (1997), and "Social Inequality III" (1999). This study is a continuation of the POLISH GENERAL SOCIAL SURVEY, 1992-1994 (ICPSR 6155).
venue: ICPSR Data Holdings

title: A quest for a pest: A Historical and Etymological Exploration of Termite-Related Terms in Modern Persian
abstract: This study aims to conduct an etymological and comparative analysis of several terms used to refer to termites in Modern Persian, as well as to explore the naming of this insect and its historical development within Indo-Iranian and Indo-European. Termites have annoyed humans throughout history, primarily due to their role in the destruction of organic materials, particularly wood. Consequently, the terminology associated with this insect not only reflects its biological and behavioral traits but also reveals cultural attitudes embedded in its naming. Employing historical and comparative linguistic methods, this research examines the words used to designate termites in Persian from both structural and semantic perspectives. The data for the study have been sourced from Dehkhoda’s Great Persian Dictionary, historical lexicons, and Indo-European etymological references. The etymological analysis reveals that concepts such as “eating,” “cutting,” and “destruction” are directly inspired by termites’ biological characteristics and are mirrored in their linguistic representation. The findings indicate that some of the terms associated with termites have been shaped by the historical interaction between the Persian language and local dialects. Additionally, the study highlights the influence of ancient religious beliefs on the naming of creatures like termites, which are often perceived as pests. These results illuminate the broader relationship between language and human interaction with nature, contributing to the understanding of historical linguistics and the cultural underpinnings of terminology.
venue: Historia i Świat

title: Kajian Nilai-Nilai Budaya pada Ragam Hias Masjid Kuno Lam Ura di Aceh Besar
abstract: The Lam Ura Ancient Mosque in Aceh Besar Regency is one of the cultural heritage sites that possesses historical significance while preserving its traditional ornamental decorations as an integral part of Acehnese cultural identity. The ornamental motifs found throughout the mosque serve not only as aesthetic elements but also embody cultural values that reflect the community's social life, religious beliefs, historical development, and artistic traditions. This study aims to examine the cultural values embedded in the ornamental decorations of the Lam Ura Ancient Mosque. The research employed a qualitative descriptive approach, with data collected through observation, interviews, and documentation. The collected data were analyzed using an interactive analysis model and interpreted through an iconographic approach and cultural value theory. The findings reveal that the mosque's ornamental decorations are predominantly composed of geometric, floral, and vine motifs, reflecting the integration of Islamic aesthetics with the distinctive characteristics of traditional Acehnese art. Beyond their decorative function, these motifs convey religious, historical, aesthetic, and cultural identity values while illustrating the process of cultural acculturation in Aceh. Therefore, the Lam Ura Ancient Mosque serves not only as a place of worship but also as an important cultural heritage site that contributes to the preservation of cultural values and provides a valuable source of knowledge for present and future generations.
venue: JURNAL RISET RUMPUN SENI DESAIN DAN MEDIA

title: Religiosity and Family Planning Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices among University Students in Uganda: A Scoping Review Protocol
abstract: eview question / Objective Overall objective: To identify, map and characterize the available evidence on religiosity and family planning knowledge, attitudes and practices among university students in Uganda. Review questions:What evidence exists on religiosity and family planning knowledge, attitudes and practices among university students in Uganda?How is religiosity conceptualized, operationalized and measured among university students?What religious beliefs, teachings, norms and values are associated with family planning?What religion-and culture-related barriers, facilitators and contextual factors influence family planning?What patter ns, gaps and methodological limitations characterize the existing evidence?Background Family planning is an important component of sexual and reproductive health and enables individuals and couples to make informed decisions about whether and when to have children and the timing and spacing of pregnancies.Among university students, family planning is particularly relevant because this life stage is characterized by increasing autonomy, evolving intimate relationships and greater responsibility for independent sexual and reproductive health decisions.Family planning knowledge, attitudes and practices among university students may be influenced by interpersonal, sociocultural, economic and structural factors, including relationship dynamics, gender norms, social approval, access to methods and services, concerns about side effects and future fertility, and beliefs about the acceptability of contraception.

title: Sacredness in the Home as Intangible Cultural Heritage: A Case Study of Historical Iranian Houses
abstract: Sacred space is commonly associated with formal places of worship and ritual settings. However, within the Islamic tradition, certain meanings and practices associated with the sacred can also be experienced and sustained within domestic life. This study aims to explain how sacredness is manifested in the Iranian–Islamic home and to examine its relationship with intangible cultural heritage. Using a qualitative, interpretive–historical approach, the study analyzes 18 historical Iranian houses based on theoretical and religious texts, historical sources, written documents, inscribed intangible cultural heritage elements, and architectural plans. The findings demonstrate that the manifestation of sacredness in the home differs from that in formal places of worship and, within domestic space, depends on the continuity of meanings, practices, and behaviors grounded in religious beliefs. Two overlapping analytical pathways were also identified: “behavioral–experiential sacredness,” in which meanings associated with the sacred are sustained through rituals, customs, and lived experience; and “behavioral–spatial sacredness,” in which spatial organization, together with behavior and experience, enables the manifestation and continuity of certain religious practices and meanings. The results further indicate that the continuity of this experience, through intergenerational transmission, continuous re-creation, self-identification, and the safeguarding of authenticity, can be analyzed within the framework of intangible cultural heritage.
venue: Heritage

title: Conceptions of God and Epistemic Mediation: A Five-Layer Model Abstract Religious
abstract: This article presents a five-layer architecture for determining the scope of epistemic revision in religious belief: formation, conception, propositional attitude, justification, and truth/reference. Its scope-dependency principle states that a finding at one layer warrants revision at another only through a specified connection; once such dependence is established, layer distinctions do not insulate the dependent claim. The architecture is not itself theistic. A worked application conditionally adopts theistic realism and analogical divine consciousness while separating creation, relation, revelation, and communicative trustworthiness. Sources are assessed through reliability, conditional independence, alternative explanations, and defeaters rather than source type. Worked cases distinguish lost corroboration from lost total support, available grounds from actual bases for belief, and false attribution from failed reference. Propositional and doxastic justification remain distinct, as do personal and public justification. The contribution is a typed assessment record and a criterion of diagnostic adequacy: an assessment of revision must identify its target, dependency, required response, and residual uncertainty. Each coordinate is task-relative and non-redundant in the worked cases. A proposition-centered checklist is equivalent only insofar as it represents these same distinctions and links; comparative practical performance remains to be tested.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Reasons for the use of traditional bonesetter in fracture care: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Traditional bonesetter (TBS) is often the primary choice in the treatment of fractures by communities, especially in rural areas, even though modern medical services are readily available. Dependence on TBS is a determinant of treatment success because improper fracture management is associated with increased morbidity and patient mortality. Meanwhile, information about why people prefer TBS is still limited. This systematic literature review aims to identify the reasons why patients prefer TBS in fracture treatment to improve understanding of the use of TBS in fracture cases. This study was systematically compiled in this review based on a literature search using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method. A total of three electronic databases were used, namely PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Scopus. The article search is arranged with the range of 2014-2024. Four of the 1009 selected articles have met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Funnel Plots were used to test effect size and heterogeneity with a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The results of the analysis of 4 articles found that the reasons for choosing TBS in the case of fracture were dominated by economic factors, trust in TBS, religious beliefs, and advice from people closest to them. Therefore, it is recommended to increase educational efforts and integrate traditional medicine with modern medicine to reduce the incidence of morbidity and mortality.
venue: Jurnal Lentera Kesehatan Masyarakat.

title: An opportunity to ‘be someone else’: the perceptions and experiences of male and female peer support workers in two US state prisons
abstract: PURPOSE: In response to the increasing numbers of older, frail and dying persons in Western prisons and associated healthcare costs, awareness of the need of high-quality peer care in correctional facilities is growing. This paper aims to describe perceptions and experiences of male and female peer caregivers in two US prisons regarding their roles. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Data were collected via focus groups with peer caregivers (n = 15) incarcerated in two US state prisons and examined using thematic analysis. FINDINGS: Three themes were identified: "motivation and benefits", "challenges and costs" and "learning" associated with caregiving. The findings point to differences between male and female caregivers' motivation to perform the roles. While male peer caregivers in the sample appeared to be motivated by issues related to identity, masculinity and religious beliefs, female peer caregivers cited the value of meaningful relationships. However, there were several similarities between male and female's daily experiences and learning needs, and both groups enjoyed intrinsic and extrinsic rewards associated with their roles. ORIGINALITY/VALUE: To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first paper to conjointly describe male and female peer caregiver views and experiences of caring for older persons or persons with life-limiting illness. Findings underscore the need for more research aimed at making explicit the varying benefits of peer caregiving behind bars, as well as policies ensuring increased training for peer caregivers and correctional staff.
venue: International Journal of Prison Health

title: Identity, Religion, and Globalization in Contemporary Baby Naming Practices: A Socio-Onomastic Study of Names in 2025–2026
abstract: This study aims to examine socio-onomastic trends in baby naming practices in Indonesia during the 2025–2026 period by focusing on issues of identity, religiosity, and globalization reflected in naming choices. The data consist of 30 baby names collected through documentation techniques from online news portals, social media platforms, and the researcher’s local environment. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach within the framework of socio-onomastics, which views personal names as linguistic phenomena closely related to social and cultural factors. Data were analyzed by identifying linguistic elements, cultural backgrounds, and social values embedded in the selected names. The findings reveal three major trends in contemporary baby naming practices. First, religiosity remains a dominant influence, reflected in the frequent use of Arabic-derived names and names carrying religious meanings. Second, globalization has significantly shaped naming patterns, as evidenced by the incorporation of linguistic elements from various languages, including English, French, Hebrew, and Sanskrit, often combined within a single name. Third, there is a growing tendency toward creative and innovative naming practices, reflecting parents’ desire to construct distinctive identities for their children. These findings suggest that baby names function not only as markers of personal identity but also as representations of cultural values, religious beliefs, social aspirations, and contemporary global orientations.
venue: Linguistik Terjemahan Sastra (LINGTERSA)

title: The Influence of Religion, Country of Origin, and United States Acculturation on Stress Coping Techniques in a Spanish-Speaking Free Clinic Population
abstract: Introduction Many Spanish-speaking individuals in the United States experience high levels of stress but disproportionately underutilize mental health services due to cultural, socioeconomic, and religious barriers in accessing culturally relevant mental health care. Methods Cross-sectional survey of Spanish-speaking adults to assess demographics, religious beliefs, and stress-coping preferences. Results Of 100 participants, 90% of participants identified as religious, with 75% reporting moderate to high religious influence on daily life. Higher religious influence correlated with a broader range of coping strategies, both faith-based (e.g., prayer, church attendance) and secular (e.g., work-related tasks, nature immersion, creative outlets). Non-religious participants primarily relied on exercise, entertainment, and socialization. Acculturation correlated with religious influence ( r [1, 99] = 0.348, p < 0.001), while country of origin was not significantly associated with particular coping strategies. Conclusion These findings suggest that religiosity is associated with an expanded breadth of coping behaviors among Spanish-speaking patients and may serve as an additional protective factor in managing stress. By defining specific mechanisms that are commonly utilized within this population, these findings inform the development of more culturally and spiritually sensitive mental health interventions. Lastly, this study reiterates the importance of tailoring support to individual levels of religiosity and acculturation.
venue: Hispanic Health Care International

title: Public attitudes and preferences on organ donation and allocation in china: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This cross-sectional study aimed to examine public attitudes toward postmortem organ donation and allocation fairness preferences in China. To this end, an online survey was administered through the Wenjuanxing platform among adults aged ≥ 18 years (N = 895). Only 15.1% of respondents had decided to donate, whereas 74.1% remained undecided; nevertheless, 73.7% would accept a donated organ if needed. Reciprocity (76.0%), first-come-first-served (70.5%), and medical urgency (65.7%) were most frequently endorsed as fair allocation principles. In the full-sample logistic regression (N = 895), positive attitudes (odds ratio [OR] = 5.65, p < 0.001), higher knowledge (OR = 1.56, p < 0.001), and knowing someone who had donated or was considering donating (OR = 1.96, p = 0.013) predicted willingness to donate. Further, a conditional analysis among decision-makers (N = 232) revealed that married status (OR = 0.18, p = 0.007), religious beliefs (OR = 0.22, p = 0.020), and higher education (OR = 1.50, p = 0.024) significantly differentiated donors from non-donors. Collectively, these findings indicate that organ donation willingness in China remains low despite broadly positive attitudes. Knowledge deficits, procedural uncertainty, and family-centered decision-making norms impede commitment, thereby underscoring the need for enhancing public education and institutional transparency.
venue: Scientific Reports

title: Sacred Groves: Ecological Significance, Emerging Threats and Conservation Strategies
abstract: Abstract: Sacred groves are forest areas that, through cultural and spiritual customs, have been protected as important repositories of ecological stability, biodiversity, and cultural heritage. They have come to play an essential role in local ecosystems due to their protection of indigenous species, maintenance of soil and water, and preservation of microclimatic balance. But these groves are increasingly threatened by various factors such as urbanization, conversion of agricultural land, modernization and market pressure, deforestation, exploitation of resources, and the loss of traditional faiths which once ensured their protection. Climate change coupled with excessive removal of biomass further accelerates the degradation of their ecological integrity. The following paper also examines an extensive set of conservation methods to enhance the resilience of sacred groves. Key activities include enhancing the scope of legal protection and governmental support, restoring community involvement and traditional methods of management, and facilitating documentation and research to guide appropriate solutions. Going forward, a balanced approach that respects both scientific knowledge and indigenous cultural traditions is needed for the successful management of sacred trees. Sacred grove conservation is important because it maintains the cultural tradition that has sustained these ecosystems for many years while protecting unique biodiversity. Increasing their protection ensures ecological resilience and maintains essential links between the natural world and cultural heritage. Keywords: Sacred groves, Ecological significance, Emerging threats, Conservation strategy, Biodiversity, Cultural and religious beliefs.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topic: Environmental and Cultural Studies in Latin America and Beyond

title: Ethical Foundations of Exchange: A Thematic Synthesis of Micro-Conduct of Market Participants in the Holy Quran
abstract: Markets depend on both informal institutions (norms and religious beliefs) and formal institutions. Historically, informal institutions have not been mapped onto modern institutional frameworks. The Holy Quran, although being a detailed source of such norms, has received little attention in this regard. This paper extends the thematic content analysis approach in Hassan (2026), focusing on verses governing market conduct and exchange. It builds on the economic categorization established in that paper and analyzes the verses categorized under "Market Regulations and Exchange". This paper takes the entire corpus of 30 Juz and 114 Surahs in Arabic with the Urdu and English translations and shortlists a total of 41 verses across 16 Surahs to deal with market conduct. This subset is then organized into five sub-themes, which are: mutual consent and contractual freedom; al-Mizan and measurement integrity; covenants, oaths, and trust; debt documentation; and the prohibited practices of riba and maysir. These clusters reflect a three-tiered institutional skeleton: what conditions are required to make an exchange permissible, what integrity requirements help make it work, and the limits defined to explain what makes an exchange legitimate. What differs from the economic framework is that the market and market regulations are seen from the lens of the Quran. This paper gives a thematic dataset of Quranic market-conduct requirements and relates them to the modern economic concepts.
venue: Journal of Language Literature & Social Affairs

title: Political Interest And Mental Health Across Generations And Religions
abstract: This study investigates the intricate relationship between political interest and mental health across generations and religions in Indonesia. The objective is to analyze how political engagement influences mental well-being and to understand the varying impacts of generational and religious contexts on these dynamics. Using a literature review methodology, the research synthesizes existing academic sources, including journal articles and studies, to provide a comprehensive overview of the topic. The findings reveal that political interest acts as both a potential source of purpose and a significant stressor. For older generations, such as Baby Boomers and Generation X, political engagement is often rooted in historical experiences of authoritarianism, leading to skepticism and selective involvement. In contrast, Millennials and Generation Z exhibit a more pragmatic approach, heavily influenced by social media, yet they face heightened anxiety and mental health challenges due to political polarization and societal pressures. Moreover, the study identifies the role of religion as a crucial factor in shaping political perceptions and mental health responses. While religious beliefs can offer emotional support, they may also contribute to internal conflicts when political and religious values clash. Overall, the research underscores the necessity of fostering a supportive political and social environment that promotes mental well-being across diverse generational and religious backgrounds, highlighting the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration between political science and psychology to address these complex issues effectively.
venue: Arsy Jurnal Studi Islam

title: Konsep Toleransi Beragama dalam Perspektif Al-Qur’an dan Implikasinya Terhadap Pendidikan Agama Islam
abstract: This study aims to examine the concept of religious tolerance from a Qur’anic perspective and analyze its implications for Islamic Religious Education (PAI). This study employs a library research method using the thematic interpretation (tafsir maudhu’i) approach. Data were obtained from the Qur’an, classical and contemporary tafsir literature, scholarly books, journal articles, and other relevant academic sources. Data were analyzed using content analysis to identify, interpret, and synthesize Qur’anic values related to religious tolerance, particularly those contained in Surah Al-Baqarah verse 256, Surah Al-Kafirun verse 6, and Surah Al-Mumtahanah verse 8. The findings indicate that religious tolerance in the Qur’an is based on three interconnected principles: freedom of religion, respect for differences in faith, and justice and good social relations with others. These principles demonstrate that tolerance in Islam does not imply mixing religious beliefs or compromising faith, but rather respecting differences while maintaining religious identity and promoting peaceful social relations. The study further finds that these Qur’anic values are highly relevant to PAI as a means of developing students’ religious character, moderation, respect for diversity, and social responsibility. However, their implementation requires contextual, dialogical, and adaptive learning approaches to address narrow and exclusive religious interpretations. This study contributes to strengthening the conceptual foundation for integrating Qur’anic values of tolerance into contemporary PAI.
venue: Islamic Education

title: A Critical Examination of Socio-Religious Interaction between Christianity and Ibibio Culture of Akwa Ibom State
abstract: Abstract The Ibibio people of Akwa Ibom State possess a rich cultural heritage embodied in their traditional religious beliefs, and culture while their indigenous worldview centred on Abasi Ibom, ancestral veneration and belief in spirits. With the advent of Christianity in Ibibioland in the 19th century, through the activities of early missionaries, a dynamics of process of cultural encounter, conflict, accommodation as well as transformation were initiated. This study underscored the socio-religious interaction between Christianity and Ibibio culture of Akwa Ibom State. This study adopted a mixed-methods approach, combining qualitative with historical designs. Data was gathered through in-depth interview and participant observation approaches. The finding revealed how Christianity has influenced and reshaped core aspects of Ibibio socio-cultural life, and on the other hand, how Ibibio culture has influenced the practice of Christianity in the area. Thus, Christian presence in Ibibioland has led to decline in certain practices considered incompatible with her doctrine but has not totally eradicated Ibibio culture. The study concluded that the interaction is not of total conflict but of continuous negotiation which prove certain elements of inculturation and syncretism resulting in Africanized Christianity. It is strongly recommended that a balanced inculturation approach that preserves positive Ibibio cultural values such as traditional language, arts, music, among others be maintained while promoting Christian moral principles for sustainable development of Ibibioland.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Influence of Greek, Egyptian, and Hindu Mythology on Human Behaviour and Morality
abstract: Mythology has been used by human cultures throughout history to make sense of death, givedeath moral meaning, and deal with the unknown. People’s stories of death and the afterlifeinfluence individual conduct, systems of ethics, and collective norms across civilisations, notmerely mirror cultural beliefs. This review discusses how three of the world’s most influentialancient mythologies, Greek, Egyptian, and Hindu, present death and the afterlife and how thesepresentations continue to inform human psychology and moral conduct. This paper uses acomparative theoretical analysis of primary mythological narratives and their associatedreligious structures to explore the ways in which beliefs about the afterlife influence deathanxiety, life satisfaction, and moral decision-making. It draws upon the figures, rituals, andcosmological frameworks embedded within each custom, including the tripartite judgment ofthe Greek underworld and the Erinyes, the weighing of the heart against the feather of Ma’at,and the karmic cycle of samsāra and the pursuit of moksha in Hinduism, to understand howdifferent spiritual systems produce distinct moral obligations. Together, these traditions revealthat while religious belief is not the only source of morality, mythological narratives are amongthe most enduring and broad structures that individuals and societies use to make sense of life,death, and the choices in between. Therefore, this paper explores the profound and multifacetedimpact of these ancient mythologies on the ethical frameworks and behavioural norms withinand across societies, examining how foundational narratives shape moral reasoning andsocietal structures.

title: The Intersection of Disability and Religiosity among Elderly Beggars: A Qualitative Inquiry in Galle City, Sri Lanka
authors: D. M. H. N. K. Dissanayake
abstract: Begging persists as a marginalized survival strategy shaped by changing socio-structural systems. In Sri Lanka, the decline of traditional extended families and a rapidly aging population have pushed vulnerable older adults into severe destitution. This qualitative study explores how physical disability and religious beliefs intersect to shape the daily experiences of elderly beggars within the Galle City administrative boundaries. Utilizing a qualitative research design, primary data were gathered through structured in-depth interviews with 15 purposely sampled elderly beggars, supplemented by secondary data for literature contextualization and qualitative descriptive data analysis. The empirical findings indicate that physical disability serves a dual, paradoxical role, it completely bars older individuals from conventional labour markets while functioning as a form of visual capital that increases personal sympathy and material donations from passersby. Concurrently, internal religiosity heavily conditions the participants' psychological coping mechanisms. Entrenched cultural beliefs in past-life karma and destiny provide existential meaning to their current suffering, yet they simultaneously in still a fatalistic framework that restricts their proactive capacity to cope, dampens their courage, and limits their ability to escape chronic street dependency. This study bridges a vital literature gap by demonstrating how structural physical limitations and internal cultural-religious systems interact to reinforce and normalize chronic socioeconomic marginalization among elderly urban populations.
venue: Journal of Social Sciences - NISD

With the advent of Christianity in Ibibioland in the 19th century, through the activities of early missionaries, a dynamics of process of cultural encounter, conflict, accommodation as well as transformation were initiated. title: Numerical Code of Culture: The Symbolism of Numbers 3, 7, and 40 in the Proverbs and Folklore Formulas of Kyrgyz and English Cultures
abstract: The article examines the symbolism of the numbers 3, 7, and 40, which are traditionally regarded as sacred in many world cultures. The study aims to identify and compare the symbolic meanings of these numbers in Kyrgyz and English linguocultural traditions. The research material comprises proverbs, folklore formulas, and set expressions documented in authoritative lexicographic sources of both languages. The goal of the work is to determine the extent to which numerical symbolism reflects the cultural and historical characteristics of a people, including their way of life, religious beliefs, and tribal traditions. The methodological framework is based on contrastive analysis, linguocultural description, and semantic analysis. The study reveals that the number 3 in both cultures is associated with completeness and sacred wholeness; however, in the Kyrgyz tradition, three people embody grace and communality, whereas in English usage, the "third wheel" often carries a negative connotation. The number 7 in Kyrgyz culture is intimately connected with ancestor veneration and genealogical memory ("zheti ata"), while in English culture, it is primarily linked to biblical symbolism and the notion of cosmic completeness. The most significant differences are found in the semantics of the number 40: in Kyrgyz culture, it permeates all major life rituals from birth to death, whereas in English, it appears rarely and almost exclusively in biblical contexts. The findings confirm that numbers in proverbs and folklore formulas function as cultural codes encoding the worldview of a people.
venue: Bulletin of Science and Practice

title: Cross-national and cross-religious variation in religiosity–forgiveness associations.
abstract: Prior research has shown that higher levels of religiosity and experiencing God/the Divine as loving and forgiving are positively associated with interpersonal forgiveness. However, many of these studies rely on samples drawn from predominantly Western nations and Westernized religions (e.g., Christianity). In the current research, we analyzed these associations using a large, religiously diverse dataset from the Global Flourishing Study (N = 202,898), which sampled participants from 22 countries and 17 religious groups. We created a latent factor for religiosity from multiple indicators and used multilevel modeling to examine associations with self-reported forgiveness. Results showed that religiosity (i.e., religious belief, bonding, and belonging) was positively associated with self-reported forgiveness. This association varied across countries and religious groups and was stronger in countries with higher (vs. lower) average levels of religiosity. Additionally, experiencing divine love was positively associated with self-reported forgiveness, but only in countries with higher (vs. lower) average levels of religiosity. Conversely, experiencing divine punishment was negatively associated with self-reported forgiveness, which was stronger in countries with lower (vs. higher) average levels of religiosity. These findings provide insight into cross-national and cross-religious variation in the associations between religiosity, divine love, divine punishment, and forgiveness across global religious and cultural contexts.
venue: Peace and Conflict Journal of Peace Psychology

title: Climate Change Adaptation Strategies Utilizing Indigenous Knowledge and Food Security: An Ethnographic Study in Pariangan Village, West Sumatra
abstract: This study investigates how the Minangkabau community specifically in Pariangan Village adapts agricultural activities to climate variability based on traditional knowledge. This includes the utilization of religious beliefs, the interpretation of natural signs, and intergenerational informal practices. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork involving interviews with 31 participants (each with a minimum of five years of farming experience) and supplemented by climatological data from Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) in 2020–2025, this research identifies significant disruptions to seasonal patterns. Consequently, the community has developed adaptation strategies, including village granaries (lumbung nagari), paddy irrigation distribution systems, mixed-garden agroforestry (parak system), mutual cooperation (gotong royong), and belief-based rituals. Thematic analysis, supported by NVivo software, reveals that environmental changes are frequently interpreted through moral and cosmological frameworks. Despite the efficacy of these practices, local mechanisms remain largely disconnected from broader development frameworks. To mitigate climate variability and strengthen food security, policymakers must formalize and integrate community-based environmental knowledge into broader climate change adaptation policies and regional development planning. Simultaneously, the general public and farming communities are encouraged to adopt adaptive, climate-smart agricultural practices and actively utilize scientific weather forecasting alongside local knowledge to build long-term environmental resilience.
venue: Proceedings of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences B Life and Environmental Sciences

title: CRITICAL DISCOURSE ANALYSIS OF CULTURAL VALUES AND BELIEFS IN SOCIETY THROUGH TEXTBOOKS
abstract: Educational system with its goals and practices is now a dominant part of civilized societies. The purpose of this study is to analyze the ideologies and fundamental values which are working behind the theoretical representation of educational policies in Pakistan. Mixed Method approach has been applied in this study. Fairclough’s 3D model is used to conduct analysis on descriptive level, interpretational level and the explanatory level (Faiclough, 1989). This study has also applied Model of Van Dijk “The socio Cognitive Analysis” for ideological analysis (Dijk, 1989). Teaching content of selected books of Punjab and NWFP Curriculum Board has been analyzed by means of critical approaches. Paper demonstrates the findings which prove that how the textbook knowledge is socially constructed. Analysis has been carried out in various dimensions including textual analysis, analyzing lexical items, indoctrination of cultural social and religious beliefs. Moreover, the awareness of educated class about biasness of text is examined and last section discusses with the results and opinion of researcher. Thus, it has been extracted that course books and textual discourse in Pakistan serves the interests of powerful fraction of society and the interests of learners are kept aside while designing syllabus. This paper is to highlight the fact that books must be designed to transmit knowledge, develop creative skills and to make learners capable, therefore they must not be bias and neither should be mean of manipulating young minds

title: Understanding Menstrual Knowledge, Attitudes, and Sociocultural Beliefs Among Adolescent Boys in Ghana: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Background: Adolescent boys often lack adequate menstrual education, leaving them susceptible to harmful sociocultural influences and reinforcing discriminatory attitudes. The purpose for this study was to explore adolescent boys’ knowledge, sociocultural beliefs, and attitudes toward menstruation. Methods: A descriptive-phenomenological qualitative study was conducted, involving 25 in-depth interviews with adolescent boys enrolled in senior high school (eligibility age range 14–19 years; achieved sample aged 15–19 years) from five districts in Ghana’s Volta Region. Participants were purposively sampled to ensure diverse perspectives. Semi-structured interviews explored knowledge sources, sociocultural influences, and attitudes toward menstruation. Data were analyzed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework with the aid of MAXQDA software. Results: Adolescent boys’ knowledge of menstruation was fragmented, stemming from family, school, and internet sources. Mothers were frequently cited as key informants, but misconceptions about menstruation persisted. Sociocultural and religious beliefs reinforced menstruation-related taboos, such as restrictions on cooking and entering sacred spaces, shaping discriminatory attitudes. Reactions to menstrual leaks varied from empathy to teasing. Conclusions: The findings highlight the need for inclusive menstrual education targeting boys and their families. Educational programs should include biological, emotional, and social aspects of menstruation to help reduce myths and nurture empathy.
